data.narrative:
Destinus is a late-stage Defense & Security company that has raised over $400M to date, founded by Mikhail Kokorich. The sector peer universe comprises 21 same-sector companies, including 2 public comparables (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private peers. Notable adjacent private companies include Anduril Industries, Helsing, and Shield AI, though none form a sufficiently tight same-stage peer cohort for reliable median multiple extraction.

Given the limited same-stage comparable set, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology applied to the $400M raised proxy. A typical late-stage step-up multiplier of 1.2x yields an implied valuation of $480M. This method is applicable where peer multiples are sparse; the step-up accounts for standard value creation expected between funding rounds at this maturity level.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $408M (low) to $552M (median of $480M), centered on the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the absence of tightly matched late-stage Defense & Security comparables—peer multiples from adjacent stages or broader sector cohorts would improve precision—and the opaque deployment of the $400M+ raised to date, which affects confidence in using total capital as a reliable valuation proxy. Additional disclosure on revenue, profitability, or customer concentration would materially narrow this range.
